steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Regular verbs: drop -en and add: -e, -st, -t, -en, -t, -en. Irregular verbs (sein, haben, werden) must be memorised. Some verbs have vowel changes (e→i, e→ie) in du/er/sie forms: sprechen → du sprichst, er spricht; sehen → du siehst, er sieht.

steps.title: Exam Tip
steps.body: With sein verbs, the past participle does NOT add a ge- prefix if the verb ends in -ieren: studieren → ich habe studiert (NOT gestudiert). Irregular past participles must be memorised: gehen → gegangen, schreiben → geschrieben, trinken → getrunken.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Regular verbs: drop -en, add -te endings: ich machte, du machtest, er machte, wir machten, ihr machtet, sie machten. The imperfect is essential for reading comprehension in the exam.

steps.title: German Exam Tips — Tenses: Present, Perfect and Imperfect
steps.body: 1. For Tenses: Present, Perfect and Imperfect, use a range of vocabulary and complex grammatical structures to access higher marks 2. Check verb tenses, agreements and word order carefully in your written work 3. In translation tasks, translate meaning rather than word-for-word 4. When writing about Tenses: Present, Perfect and Imperfect, include opinions and justifications, not just descriptions 5. For listening and reading, focus on key words and cognates to extract meaning

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Conjugate "spielen" in the present and perfect tenses for "ich" and "er/sie". | Q: When do you use sein vs haben as the auxiliary in the perfect tense?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Present: ich spiele, er/sie spielt. Perfect: ich habe gespielt, er/sie hat gespielt. | Use sein for: (1) verbs of movement (gehen, fahren, laufen, fliegen, kommen), (2) verbs of change of state (aufwachen, sterben, werden), (3) sein and bleiben. Use haben for all other verbs (most verbs

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Use a range of tenses (present, past, future) to access higher marks Include opinions with reasons (ich finde... weil... / meiner Meinung nach...) Check case endings (nominative, accusative, dative) before finishing Get word order right: verb-second in main clauses, verb-at-end after dass/weil/wenn Use complex structures: subordinate clauses, modal verbs, separable verbs Include cultural references to German-speaking countries (DACH)
